sections.title: Prerequisite: The Basis Vectors
lecture_lines: 3D space uses unit vectors î, ĵ, k̂.
Every vector is a combination of these.
Imagine these as anchors for space.
animations: Create unit vectors i-hat and j-hat at (1,0) and (0,1). Color: #FFD700 (Gold).
Flash vectors i-hat and j-hat one by one to highlight basis.
Draw a 2D grid behind the basis vectors. Color: #A9A9A9 (DarkGray).

sections.title: Defining Linear Transformation
lecture_lines: Linear means grid lines stay parallel.
The origin always remains fixed here.
animations: Show a linear grid deformation. Color: #FFFFFF (White).
Highlight that parallel grid lines remain parallel. Color: #FF4500 (OrangeRed).
Show the origin remains fixed at (0,0). Color: #00FFFF (Cyan).

sections.title: The Transformation Matrix (The 'Recipe')
lecture_lines: Matrix columns show where basis lands.
This defines the entire space transformation.
Think of it as a movement recipe.
The robot arm tracks its axes.
Final positions form the matrix columns.
animations: Display matrix [[a, b], [c, d]]. Color: #FFFFFF (White).
Animate i-hat landing at (a, c). Color: #FFD700 (Gold).
Animate j-hat landing at (b, d). Color: #FFD700 (Gold).
Highlight the matrix columns as the landing spots. Color: #00FF00 (Lime).
Overlay the matrix on the grid transformation. Color: #FFFFFF (White).

sections.title: Visualizing Rotation and Scaling
lecture_lines: Scaling alters the basis vector lengths.
Rotation changes direction, keeping orthogonality intact.
Matrices represent these precise spatial changes.
Model growth is a scaling matrix.
Character turns use a rotation matrix.
animations: Rotate the grid by 90 degrees counter-clockwise. Color: #FF4500 (OrangeRed).
Scale the grid by a factor of 2. Color: #00FFFF (Cyan).
Show rotation and scaling occurring simultaneously. Color: #FFFFFF (White).
Display the transformation matrix for rotation. Color: #FFD700 (Gold).
Display the transformation matrix for scaling. Color: #FFD700 (Gold).

sections.title: Determinants: The Volume Factor
lecture_lines: Determinants represent the volume scale factor.
A shrinkage means a smaller determinant.
animations: Show a unit square area defined by vectors i and j. Color: #00FF00 (Lime).
Deform the square into a parallelogram. Color: #FF4500 (OrangeRed).
Highlight the new area of the parallelogram. Color: #FFFFFF (White).
Show the determinant value as the area scaling factor. Color: #FFD700 (Gold).
Visualize negative determinant (flipping orientation). Color: #FF0000 (Red).
